title: JavaScript Deep Dive
tagline: V8 engine internals, prototype chains, memory profiling, and modern ESNext standards
description: From call stack execution contexts and event loop phases to prototype delegation, typed arrays, memory leaks, and high-performance JavaScript engines.

stages.title: Stage 1: Engine Internals & Memory Model
stages.description: How V8 parses, compiles (Ignition & TurboFan), manages memory, and executes code.

nodes.title: V8 JIT Compilation, Hidden Classes & Inline Caching
nodes.description: How V8 compiles JS to bytecode with Ignition, optimizes hot code with TurboFan, and uses hidden classes (Shapes) for fast property access.
nodes.whyItMatters: Writing monomorphic functions with consistent object shapes allows the JIT compiler to inline properties and achieve C++-like performance.

resources.title: V8 Dev Blog: Fast Properties in V8

keyTakeaways: Avoid adding or deleting properties dynamically on objects after instantiation to preserve hidden classes.
Initialize all fields in constructor functions in the same order.
Understand deoptimizations (deopts) caused by polymorphic argument types.
nodes.interviewTips: Senior roles love questions on how V8 optimizes object property lookup and what causes JIT deoptimization.

nodes.title: Garbage Collection & Memory Leak Diagnostics
nodes.description: Mark-and-sweep GC algorithm, heap snapshots in Chrome DevTools, retained memory trees, closures, and detached DOM nodes.
nodes.whyItMatters: Single-page applications that run for hours or days without reloading crash the browser tab if event listeners or caches leak memory.
keyTakeaways: Uncleaned setInterval timers and forgotten event listeners hold references to outer scopes.
Use WeakMap and WeakSet when associating metadata with objects without preventing garbage collection.
Compare before-and-after heap snapshots to identify detached DOM elements.
nodes.interviewTips: Be prepared to diagnose a simulated memory leak and explain the difference between Shallow Size and Retained Size.

stages.title: Stage 2: Closures, Prototypes & Object Delegation
stages.description: Lexical scoping, closure memory costs, prototype inheritance, and modern ES classes.

nodes.title: Prototypes & Lexical Scope Closures
nodes.description: How the prototype chain delegation (__proto__, Object.getPrototypeOf) works and how functions retain lexical scope environments.
nodes.whyItMatters: Misunderstanding closures leads to unexpected variable capture in loops. Prototypes are the fundamental inheritance model of JavaScript.

resources.title: You Don't Know JS: Scope & Closures
MDN Inheritance and the prototype chain

keyTakeaways: A closure is formed whenever a function accesses variables outside its immediate lexical scope.
JavaScript objects do not copy parent methods; they delegate lookups up the prototype chain until null is reached.
Modern `class` syntax is syntactic sugar over prototypal inheritance.
nodes.interviewTips: You will almost certainly be asked to implement a debounce or throttle function using closures, or explain `this` binding in arrow vs regular functions.
